rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Name and business, stranger. You say you are new here; state your purpose.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Name and business, stranger. I have no task for you.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Name your business, stranger. I have no answer for that.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Name your business, stranger. I have no advice to give you.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Name and business, stranger.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: That is your choice, stranger. Keep to your business and I will keep to mine.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Well now. New to the place, are you?

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Well now, offering help to a guard on patrol. What sort of hand did you have in mind?

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Well now. Captain Roderic? Strict, but fair.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Well now, asking a gate guard for advice. That’s a tidy bit of timing, isn’t it?

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Well now, you’ve found a sunny patch to stand in, at least. Better than rain on the west approach.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Well now, you don't have to. I'm only asking a question, not asking for your trust.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: You’re new, are you? Keep to the road and don’t make trouble.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: A hand? No. Keep yours where I can see them and move along.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: The captain? What’s that to you?

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Into the city? Ask someone else. I’ve nothing for you.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Weather. Keep moving.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Trust me? You shouldn't. Keep your distance and answer plainly.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Oh, love, this is my inn yard. I'm keeping it in hand while the kitchen waits on water.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Oh, love, that's kind of you to ask. I'm managing the yard just now.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Oh, love, I’ve no read on the captain to give you. Now, if you’ll excuse me, this yard won’t tend itself.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Oh, love, I’ve no advice to give you on that. Now, if you’ll excuse me, this yard won’t tend itself.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Oh, love, it is—makes tending the yard a pleasure, for once.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Oh, love, you needn’t trust me yet. I’ve got a yard to tend and hungry travellers to feed; you can judge me by what you see.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: If you're buying, speak. I don't know you, and I'm working.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: What. If you know smithing, put your hands to work; if not, don't get in my way.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: What about him? I’ve work to finish.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: What. I’m working; ask someone who knows the city.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: What. Weather won't mend iron.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: You shouldn't. I don't know you, and I've no use for talk that doesn't hold up under a hammer.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Oh! You’re new? I’m Jory, and I’m helping at the forge—but I don’t know what to call this place, sorry, I’ve been at the anvil most of the day.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Oh! Maybe—though Aunt Mara says I ought to keep my hands on the scrap, and I’m already helping around the forge. What sort of hand did you mean?

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Oh! The captain? I don't know him well enough to say, and I shouldn't go guessing—but what have you heard?

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Oh! The city? I don't know anything about getting in, I'm only at the forge, but—are you going there for something?

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Oh, is it? I was watching the forge and missed it—what’s it like out there?

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Oh! You don't have to, I suppose—but I'm not trying to trick you. I'm just helping at the forge, and I ask a lot of questions.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Mind the timber. I couldn't tell you; I'm keeping to my work.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Keep clear of the timber, if you would. I’ve got my hands full here.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Mind the timber. The captain keeps his eye on the work; I’ll keep mine on the beam.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Mind the timber. I’ve nothing useful to tell you about getting in.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Mm. The timber's still waiting on a sound lift.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Trust is your measure to take. I’ll keep to the work in front of me.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Friend! New to these roads, are you? A question like that is worth a question in return: what brings you here?

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Friend, a hand has its value—but I’ve no bargain to put before you just now.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Friend, I make no trade in opinions about the captain. What value would that bring either of us?

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Friend, advice has its price—and you’ve not offered me a bargain worth answering yet.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Friend! Fine enough for trade, wouldn't you say?

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Friend, trust is a wager. What would make the risk worth it to you?

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: New here. I see. I have the south road to watch.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Stranger. Hands free, by the look of them. Nothing to report.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Mud on your boots. You ask about the captain; I’ve nothing to report on him.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Stranger. You need the city. I have no advice for you.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Clear skies. I can see the south road well.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: You shouldn't. I'm watching the south road. I report what I see.

rows.stranger: Good day. I'm new here; what is this place?
rows.line: Hm. New, are you.

rows.stranger: Could you use a hand with anything?
rows.line: Hm. Keep walking.

rows.stranger: What do you make of the captain?
rows.line: Hm. Captain's the captain.

rows.stranger: I need to get into the city. Any advice?
rows.line: Hm. Ask someone else.

rows.stranger: Fine weather, isn't it?
rows.line: Hm. Weather.

rows.stranger: Why should I trust you?
rows.line: Hm. Don’t, then.
